title: Defect-induced optical magnons and local magnetic correlations in MnSb2Te4
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, S. X. M. Riberolles, D. M. Pajerowski, Jiaqiang Yan, R. J. McQueeney
abstract: Magnetic defect engineering offers a route to manipulate and control magnetic and electronic states in quantum materials. In the Mn(Bi,Sb)2Te4 family of topological magnetic insulators, Sb substitution facilitates site mixing between Mn and Sb atoms that affects magnetic order and band topology. Here we directly probe these defect-induced magnetic interactions using inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of MnSb2Te4. We find that antisite mixing generates inequivalent and disordered magnetic sublattices where strong defect-induced antiferromagnetic coupling produces an optical magnon with a large gap. Semi-classical spin-dynamics simulations accurately capture magnetic excitations in the ordered and paramagnetic states and identify that linear Mn-Te-Mn bonds mediate coupling to antisite magnetic defects.
summary: This work investigates how structural defects, specifically antisite mixing, modify the magnetic properties of topological magnetic insulators like $	ext{MnSb}_2	ext{Te}_4$. By combining inelastic neutron scattering with spin-dynamics simulations, the authors demonstrate that these defects induce a strong, measurable antiferromagnetic coupling responsible for an observable optical magnon gap. This highlights defect engineering as a powerful tool to tune fundamental magnetic interactions in quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to directly probe defect-induced magnetic interactions and understand how antisite mixing affects the spin dynamics of topological magnetic insulators.
main_result: Antisite mixing generates disordered sublattices, leading to a distinct optical magnon mode with a large gap ($\Delta' \approx 1.5$ meV), indicating strong defect-mediated antiferromagnetic coupling ($J'$).
method: The research combines inelastic neutron scattering (INS) experiments on single crystals with semi-classical spin-dynamics simulations using Landau-Lifshitz Dynamics (LLD).
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{MnSb}_2	ext{Te}_4$, a topological magnetic insulator in the $	ext{Mn}(	ext{Bi},	ext{Sb})_2	ext{Te}_4$ family, which exhibits significant antisite defects. The analysis uses spin Hamiltonians incorporating various exchange couplings ($J_0, J_c, J'$).
key_observables: Optical magnon gap ($\Delta'$), spin wave dispersion curves (acoustic and optic branches), magnetic dimer structure factor.
important_parameters: Defect concentration ($\sim 15\%$ in MST vs. $<3\%$ in MBT); coupling strengths ($J' \approx 0.7$ meV, $J_0 = -0.075$ meV).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed optical magnon mode is a signature of defect-induced ferrimagnetism and relies on fitting spin wave dispersions to model parameters.
figures_summary: Figures show INS data (constant energy slices, in-plane dispersion) for MST compared to MBT, illustrating the distinct magnetic excitation spectrum caused by defects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the problem of defect influence in topological insulators to presenting experimental INS measurements, followed by theoretical modeling using spin Hamiltonians and LLD simulations to quantify the defect-induced couplings.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how disorder (antisite defects) fundamentally alters the magnetic Hamiltonian and excitation spectrum of a quantum material, which is relevant for understanding engineered correlated states in condensed matter systems.
